findings.reason: §2's write target and §4's central reuse justification both rest on a layout the plan itself records as superseded, so the next node would write and load through the wrong path.
findings.text: §2 writes "the equilibrium joins the other five IDSs in /work/projects/imas_gpu/jt60sa/ids/101154/" and §4 justifies the reuse of `scripts/figures_jt60sa_geometry.py` because it "opens a directory of {ids}.nc files" and "a minted directory has that same layout" (plan.html:112–119, mirroring the loader `_read_ids` at scripts/figures_jt60sa_geometry.py:45–50 and the writer `out_dir / f"{ids_name}.nc"` at packages/imas-alambic/src/imas_alambic/pulse_mint.py:335); the plan's own comment `c-20261007T0400-jtfm-run-file` (plan.html:227) records a lead-decided move to one netCDF per run, `ids/<pulse>/<run>.nc`, states that "Two places in this plan assume today's layout" and that §4's reuse argument "needs restating" — the owning mechanism is the run-file writer whose layout the catalogue already carries as `description_store_layout` (packages/imas-alambic/src/imas_alambic/machine_map.py:1121) and which the plan should name rather than restate as a literal path

findings.reason: the exact command §5 makes its gate would fail as a missing-path error at dispatch, so §5 must name the file that exists or declare the rename a prerequisite.
findings.text: §5's done-when runs `pytest ... tests/data/test_pulse_writer.py` and names `test_write_covers_every_description_ids`, but that file does not exist in the tree (the file is `tests/data/test_pulse_mint.py` and the test is `test_mint_writes_every_description_ids`, tests/data/test_pulse_mint.py:94); §5 says the file is renamed by `jt60sa-facility-mint` §7, a rename that has not landed and that §5 neither waits on nor lists as a dependency

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — §1 is a single owner (`mint_pulse` in packages/imas-alambic/src/imas_alambic/pulse_mint.py) and §2/§4 add no new module family, delegating topology to existing finders.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — §2 and §4 hardcode the written-IDS directory layout in prose instead of resolving it through the mechanism that owns it.
rubric_items.interface_budget: pass — public_definitions 0, cli_options 0, mcp_views 0, refusal_families 0; §4 adds one CLI option and its own text states it retires nothing because the script takes no options today and a pulse is a new input.
rubric_items.reuse_search: a finding — the plan's finder census is verified against the tree, but §5 names a test file that does not exist in the codebase it extends.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — §4 extends `scripts/figures_jt60sa_geometry.py` and states in its own text why a second output of that driver beats a parallel script, retiring nothing.
